mathematical_sources.note: The formalized paper, researched under the author's direction with GPT-5.6-Sol and GPT-6-Astra and written with GPT-6-Astra, Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Argon. Statements are matched with Lean declarations in docs/PAPER-CORRESPONDENCE.md. The posted TeX source of hexagon:2611.00207v1 is byte-identical to the formalized version (SHA-256 in docs/MANUSCRIPT.md).
mathematical_sources.title: Pretorsion theories and image-closed subcategories

mathematical_sources.note: Source of the q-Gandhi polynomials of the first kind B_m, defined in Statement.lean by the recurrence of Definition 1.1 of the paper. The specialization B_m(1,1) = g_{2m+2} is not formalized.
mathematical_sources.title: q-Polynômes de Gandhi et statistique de Denert

mathematical_sources.note: Source of the q-Gandhi polynomials of the second kind C_m, defined in Statement.lean by the recurrence of Definition 1.1 of the paper. The specialization C_m(1,1) = H_{2m+1} is not formalized.
mathematical_sources.title: On a q-sequence that generalizes the median Genocchi numbers

mathematical_sources.location: J. Pure Appl. Algebra 225 (2021), no. 2, Paper No. 106503
mathematical_sources.note: Definition 2.6 there is the paper's Definition 2.2, stated in Lean for an arbitrary category; Propositions 2.1–2.2 there (the paper's Lemma 2.11) are proved in the library. The notion was introduced by Facchini and Finocchiaro (Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. 199 (2020), 1073–1089).
mathematical_sources.title: Pretorsion theories in general categories

mathematical_sources.note: Shows that the first and second components of pretorsion theories in mod Λ are the quotient-closed and submodule-closed subcategories, and lists the 17 pretorsion theories for type A_2. The closure properties used by the paper (Lemma 2.6 and Proposition 2.8 there; the paper's Proposition 2.3) are proved in the library.
mathematical_sources.title: Lattices of pretorsion classes

mathematical_sources.note: Proposition 4.10(i), Z is image-closed iff Z = Gen Z ∩ Cogen Z, is part of Theorem A and is proved in the library; splitting projective and injective objects (Section 2) are used in Section 4.3.
mathematical_sources.title: Preprojective modules over Artin algebras

mathematical_sources.note: Motivates counting subcategories by their number of indecomposables, and supplies the convex geometry of quotient and submodule closure extended in Section 4.3; its formalization is listed under related_formalizations.
mathematical_sources.title: An equidistribution conjecture for quotient-closed and submodule-closed subcategories

mathematical_sources.note: Also obtains the count H_{2n+3} for intersection-closed interval families, which correspond to image-closed subcategories of mod Λ_n by Theorem 5.5. Not used in the proofs.
mathematical_sources.title: Plumbing bijections

related_formalizations.note: 14 modules adapted for Section 4.3 (convex geometries, indecomposable skeletons, anti-exchange, relative split projectives and injectives), from commit 20ee4b9; see VENDORED.md and verification/module-origins.json.

2 modules (indecomposable modules and Fitting's lemma; idempotents of local rings) from the development state of commit eeb5b4b (not a published revision), through quotient-submodule-equidistribution, with copyright headers kept; see VENDORED.md.
